title: The Museum of Good Reasons

sourceEvidence.locator: Mara Veld is hired after objecting
sourceEvidence.excerpt: Mara Veld is hired after objecting to a school label claiming that humanity invented light. The lamp burns only because oil, land, labor, transport, maintenance, and oxygen remain outside the exhibit. Director Calistrat Orven recognizes her talent but immediately complicates it: adding oil is itself another chosen boundary. Mara’s work becomes a search for sentences that neither flatten complexity nor help wounds disguise themselves. Her personal grief matters because the museum holds connection

hook: The explanation is reasonable, but someone has still lost something.
readerPromise: This philosophical novel turns familiar objects into unsettling questions about the stories we accept. Enter the galleries, and see how long a truthful sentence can keep an injury out of sight.
protectedRevelations: Family disaster connections, archive struggle, reforms and psychedelic coda
